concepts.description_formal: For a series with terms a sub n, the nth partial sum S sub n is the sum of a sub 1 through a sub n, and the sequence of partial sums is the object whose limit defines the sum.
concepts.description_plain: The first n terms of a series add to a number that depends on n.
concepts.name: Partial sums of an infinite series
concepts.notation: a sub n; S sub n; sigma notation

concepts.description_formal: A series converges to S if and only if the limit of its sequence of partial sums exists and equals S; otherwise the series diverges.
concepts.description_plain: A series converges when its running totals settle on a single number.
concepts.name: Convergence of a series as a limit of its partial sums
concepts.notation: limit of S sub n; sum equals S

concepts.description_formal: A series is geometric when the quotient of consecutive terms is a constant r, so the terms are a, a r, a r squared, and so on.
concepts.description_plain: A geometric series multiplies by the same number to get from one term to the next.
concepts.name: Geometric series and the constant ratio
concepts.notation: a for the first term, r for the common ratio

concepts.description_formal: If the absolute value of r is less than one, the geometric series with first term a sums to a divided by one minus r; otherwise it diverges.
concepts.description_plain: A geometric series adds to a finite total exactly when the ratio is smaller than one in size.
concepts.name: Convergence condition and sum of a geometric series
concepts.notation: a over (1 minus r); absolute value of r less than one

concepts.description_formal: If the limit of a sub n is not zero, or fails to exist, the series diverges; a limit of zero leaves the question open.
concepts.description_plain: If the terms do not shrink to zero the total cannot settle, but shrinking terms prove nothing.
concepts.name: The nth term test as a one directional test
concepts.notation: limit of a sub n; test for divergence

concepts.description_formal: If f is positive, decreasing, and continuous on the relevant interval and a sub n equals f of n, the series and the improper integral of f converge together or diverge together.
concepts.description_plain: A series of terms read off a positive decreasing continuous function converges exactly when the matching improper integral does.
concepts.name: The integral test and its hypotheses
concepts.notation: improper integral; positive, decreasing, continuous

concepts.description_formal: The harmonic series diverges, the alternating harmonic series converges, and the p-series with terms one over n to the p converges exactly when p is greater than one.
concepts.description_plain: A short list of standard series whose behaviour is known and used as a reference.
concepts.name: Harmonic series, alternating harmonic series, and p-series
concepts.notation: p-series; harmonic series

concepts.description_formal: The form of a sub n, whether it is a constant ratio, a rational expression, a factorial or power, an alternating factor, or a term read off a function, cues the test that settles it.
concepts.description_plain: Read the shape of the general term and pick the test it fits.
concepts.name: Selection of a convergence test from the form of the terms
concepts.notation: test selection; decision cues

concepts.description_formal: For series with nonnegative terms, if a sub n is at most b sub n for all n and the series of b sub n converges, then the series of a sub n converges; if a sub n is at least b sub n and the series of b sub n diverges, then the series of a sub n diverges.
concepts.description_plain: A series squeezed under a convergent one converges, and a series above a divergent one diverges.
concepts.name: Direct comparison of series with nonnegative terms
concepts.notation: term-by-term inequality

concepts.description_formal: If the limit of a sub n over b sub n is a positive finite number, the two series of nonnegative terms converge together or diverge together.
concepts.description_plain: Two series whose terms have a positive finite ratio in the limit behave alike.
concepts.name: Limit comparison of series with nonnegative terms
concepts.notation: limit of the ratio; L positive and finite

concepts.description_formal: If the terms alternate in sign, decrease in absolute value, and have limit zero, the series converges.
concepts.description_plain: An alternating series converges when its term sizes shrink steadily to zero.
concepts.name: The alternating series test and its two conditions
concepts.notation: negative one to the n; decreasing in absolute value

concepts.description_formal: If the limit of the absolute value of a sub n plus one over a sub n is less than one the series converges absolutely, if it is greater than one the series diverges, and if it equals one the test is inconclusive.
concepts.description_plain: Compare the size of consecutive terms in the limit and read off convergence, divergence, or nothing.
concepts.name: The ratio test and its three cases
concepts.notation: limit of the ratio; L less than one

concepts.description_formal: If the series of absolute values converges, the series converges absolutely; absolute convergence implies convergence, and regrouping or rearranging the terms leaves the value unchanged.
concepts.description_plain: A series whose absolute values add to a finite total converges, and its value is unaffected by rearrangement.
concepts.name: Absolute convergence and its consequences
concepts.notation: series of absolute values

concepts.description_formal: A series converges conditionally when it converges but the series of absolute values diverges; the three exclusive outcomes are absolutely convergent, conditionally convergent, and divergent.
concepts.description_plain: A series can converge while the series of its absolute values diverges.
concepts.name: Conditional convergence as a separate classification
concepts.notation: conditionally convergent; absolutely convergent

concepts.description_formal: If an alternating series converges by the alternating series test, the absolute difference between the value of the series and its nth partial sum is at most the absolute value of the first omitted term.
concepts.description_plain: For a series that converges by the alternating series test, the error in a partial sum is no larger than the first term left out.
concepts.name: The alternating series error bound
concepts.notation: error at most the first omitted term

concepts.description_formal: The coefficient of the nth degree term of the Taylor polynomial for f about x equals a is the nth derivative of f at a divided by n factorial.
concepts.description_plain: Each coefficient comes from a derivative at the centre divided by a factorial.
concepts.name: Taylor polynomial coefficients from derivative values
concepts.notation: T sub n of x; f superscript n of a over n factorial

concepts.description_formal: Taylor polynomials for f about x equals a approximate values of f near a, and in many cases higher degree polynomials approach f over an interval.
concepts.description_plain: Near the centre the polynomial value stands in for the function value.
concepts.name: Taylor polynomials as approximations near the centre
concepts.notation: approximation near the centre

concepts.description_formal: The error of the nth degree Taylor polynomial at x is at most the maximum of the absolute value of the n plus first derivative on the interval between a and x, multiplied by the absolute value of x minus a to the n plus first power, divided by n plus one factorial.
concepts.description_plain: The error of a Taylor polynomial is no larger than a term built from a bound on the next derivative.
concepts.name: The Lagrange error bound
concepts.notation: max of the next derivative; (n+1) factorial

concepts.description_formal: The alternating series error bound applies when the series alternates with terms decreasing to zero; otherwise a Taylor approximation is bounded with the Lagrange form.
concepts.description_plain: Two bounds are available and the hypotheses decide which one applies.
concepts.name: Choosing between the Lagrange and alternating series bounds
concepts.notation: error bound selection

concepts.description_formal: A power series has the form the sum of a sub n times x minus r to the n, where the a sub n are real numbers and r is the centre.
concepts.description_plain: A power series is built from powers of x minus a fixed number.
concepts.name: Power series and their centre
concepts.notation: centre r; coefficients a sub n

concepts.description_formal: Applying the ratio test to a power series and requiring the limit to be less than one yields an inequality in the absolute value of x minus r whose bound is the radius of convergence.
concepts.description_plain: The ratio test turns a power series into an inequality that bounds the distance from the centre.
concepts.name: Radius of convergence from the ratio test
concepts.notation: R; open interval of radius R

concepts.description_formal: The radius gives an open interval on which the series converges, and each endpoint must be tested separately to determine whether it belongs to the interval of convergence.
concepts.description_plain: The two ends of the interval have to be checked one at a time with a suitable test.
concepts.name: Endpoint testing and the interval of convergence
concepts.notation: interval of convergence; endpoint series

concepts.description_formal: The Taylor series for f about a has nth term the nth derivative of f at a divided by n factorial times x minus a to the n, and a Taylor polynomial is a partial sum of it.
concepts.description_plain: The Taylor series continues the polynomial pattern without stopping.
concepts.name: Taylor series and the general term
concepts.notation: general term; partial sum of the series

concepts.description_formal: The Maclaurin series for one over one minus x is geometric, and the Maclaurin series for the exponential, the sine, and the cosine are the foundation for building other series.
concepts.description_plain: Four series are recalled rather than rederived.
concepts.name: The standard Maclaurin series
concepts.notation: e to the x, sin x, cos x, one over one minus x

concepts.description_formal: Differentiating or integrating a power series term by term produces a new power series representing the derivative or an antiderivative of the original function.
concepts.description_plain: A power series can be differentiated or integrated one term at a time.
concepts.name: Term-by-term differentiation and integration of a power series
concepts.notation: term-by-term differentiation; term-by-term integration

concepts.description_formal: A series obtained by term-by-term differentiation or integration has the same radius of convergence as the original, while the behaviour at the endpoints must be determined separately.
concepts.description_plain: The derived series reaches just as far, but the ends may behave differently.
concepts.name: Radius preserved and endpoints rechecked
concepts.notation: same radius; endpoints retested
